note: Working name (Q33). The small alphabet of A. W. N. Pugin, Glossary of Ecclesiastical Ornament (1844), plate 9 ('Alphabets No. 1'; the book's Plate X), which Pugin dates to the latter part of the fifteenth century. A textura minuscule written with a broad nib, every letter drawn with hairline flourishes. Plain forms are built from the same nib strokes and are the defaults; Pugin's flourished forms are alternates (decision 0008, decision 0011, brief 2026-10-28-textura-start).
zone_note: the lowercase rows on the flattened plate, inside the frame and below the capitals
body_note: an opening this wide removes the hairlines (about 7 px) and keeps the nib's strokes (38 px and more): what is left is each letter's body
glyphs_note: Each box (flattened-plate pixels) holds the centre of the letter's larger body pieces, which seed it; every other piece of ink, hairlines and swashes included, goes to the letter it is joined to by the shortest way along the ink. The ampersand is hairline only: the middle of its box seeds it.

spacing.note: As the Lombardic's (tools/type/spacing.py), over the x-height, but with the target white set so two i's stand one minim's pitch apart (the pitch of n's stems): a textura is spaced like a fence. The pairs still off are kerned; nothing may come closer than the clearance over the whole height, ascenders and descenders included. Provisional.
